### Overall achievements
Using satellite observations from multiple sources, UAV remote-sensing data, and field expedition measurements, we developed geometric standardization and radiometric normalization techniques for long-term, multi-scale, multi-source satellite data, together with coordinated space–air–ground methods for retrieving key ecosystem parameters. We produced long-term satellite ready-to-use (RTU) datasets for the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau at multiple resolutions and with high accuracy, as well as 24 remote-sensing products across five categories of key ecosystem parameters. These cover vegetation structure and growth, the carbon cycle, land-surface energy, water properties and distribution, and human activities. The products span spatial resolutions of 500 m to 0.8 m and the period from the 1970s to 2023, providing reliable data for assessing ecosystem services and their changing trends on the plateau.

### Overall achievements
We completed the CASEarth DataBank system, integrating data, computing, and services. We also built a multi-source satellite data processing and integration service supporting on-demand processing of 18 types of remote-sensing data products, and a quality inspection system supporting 22 types of domestic and international Earth observation satellite data and products.
The long-term Landsat RTU collection covers China and surrounding areas from the 1980s onward. It includes 12 products: surface reflectance, land-surface temperature, top-of-atmosphere reflectance, at-satellite brightness temperature, NDVI, EVI, MSAVI, SAVI, NDWI, NDMI, NBR, and FVC, with approximately 645,000 scenes and 7.74 million data products overall. We produced 14 global 30 m map editions for the 1980s, 1985s, 1990s, 1995s, 2000s, 2005s, 2010s, 2011s, 2013s, 2015s, 2017s, 2018s, 2019s, and 2021s, as well as six nationwide 2 m map editions for 2016s, 2018s, 2019s, 2020s, 2021s, and 2022s. Products at resolutions down to sub-meter scale were supplied for selected areas according to project and external requirements. Data submission has been completed in accordance with CAS scientific data management requirements and the project's data-sharing arrangements, with a total volume of approximately 2.9 PB.

### Long-term multi-source Earth observation RTU products

#### (1) Long-term Landsat RTU products for China and surrounding areas

These products have been used by more than 30 research institutes, universities, and application organizations. Users include the CAS Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, Institute of Botany, Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography, Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, and Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment; Tsinghua University, Peking University, Fudan University, Wuhan University, Shenzhen University, and China University of Geosciences; France's ENSAS school of architecture; the Research Institute of Forest Resource Information Techniques of the Chinese Academy of Forestry; and Sungrow Renewables. Applications span agriculture, forestry, land resources, ecology and the environment, and energy.

#### (2) Multi-source high-resolution RTU products

The nationwide 2 m map supports demonstrations of the Digital Earth science platform. Products for selected areas at resolutions down to sub-meter scale have supported platform demonstrations and SDG demonstration zones in Hainan and Lincang.

#### (3) Global thematic products at 30 m resolution

The global 30 m land-surface water product was incorporated into the Global Water Resources Data Products collection of the International Research Center of Big Data for Sustainable Development and released internationally in March 2023. It supports monitoring and assessment of water-related Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 6.6, SDG 11, SDG 13, and SDG 15, and contributes to sustainable water resource management. CASEarth DataBank provides bulk download, online visualization, and other services to make the global product easier to share and use.

Forest cover research was included in both the 2020 and 2021 editions of the Big Earth Data in Support of the Sustainable Development Goals reports, edited by Academician Huadong Guo and published in Chinese and English. The forest product was selected as an SDG public data product. Its research case was exhibited at the International Forum on Big Data for Sustainable Development and featured on the SDG big data platform homepage, where on-demand production of SDG 15.1.1 forest cover data and assessment of forest coverage were implemented.

To support China's science diplomacy, the 2020 global 30 m forest cover product was included in the BRICS Sustainable Development Data Products collection at the BRICS Forum on Big Data for Sustainable Development, held in Beijing on April 26–27, 2022. It supported Xinhua's news video on viewing BRICS from space and was released as a core output. In October 2022, the global 30 m forest cover product was again selected for the global sustainable development data products presented by CBAS to the United Nations, and was presented by State Councilor and Foreign Minister Wang Yi.

Burned area research cases were included in the 2020 and 2021 editions of the Big Earth Data in Support of the Sustainable Development Goals reports in Chinese and English. They were exhibited at the CAS exhibition on Big Earth Data for monitoring and assessing the SDGs, organized with the SDG center and other partners to mark the 50th anniversary of the restoration of the People's Republic of China's lawful seat in the United Nations. At the request of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, we submitted a report on high-resolution monitoring of burned area changes in Australia (2005–2019), based on the long-term 30 m burned area product, to support relevant decisions with data and information.

At the ministerial meeting of the Group of Friends of the Global Development Initiative on September 20, 2022, State Councilor and Foreign Minister Wang Yi presented the burned area product to the United Nations to support countries in achieving the SDGs. The product was also included in the UN Biodiversity Lab (UNBL) data-sharing platform.

\n1月7日，《自然》（Nature）期刊在线发表了题为“小规模持续的湿润森林损:
On January 7, Nature published the paper "Small persistent humid forest clearings drive tropical forest biomass losses" online. Using high-resolution forest disturbance and biomass data, the study constructed a grid-scale database of vegetation recovery following forest disturbances, then developed a forest carbon bookkeeping model integrating the database with high-resolution remote-sensing observations. The model was used to estimate spatial and temporal changes in vegetation carbon stocks caused by forest disturbances from 1990 to 2020, and to quantify the contributions of different disturbance types and patch sizes to changes in forest vegetation carbon stocks and carbon density. By introducing spatially explicit carbon recovery curves, the model overcomes the traditional reliance on regional response curves and substantially improves the representation of spatial heterogeneity and disturbance responses. The first author is Yidi Xu, a postdoctoral researcher at France's Laboratory for Climate and Environmental Sciences (LSCE). The co-corresponding authors are Wei Li, an associate professor in the Department of Earth System Science at Tsinghua University, and Philippe Ciais, a professor at LSCE. Guojin He, a researcher at the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences, is a co-author.

The long-term global 30 m burned area product (GABAM), developed by Guojin He's research team, including Zhaoming Zhang and Tengfei Long, provided key supporting data. It enabled precise characterization of tropical forest fire disturbances over the past 30 years, particularly small burned patches, and helped quantify tropical forest carbon losses.

Since 2016, with support from projects under the National Key Research and Development Program of China and other programs, Guojin He's team has developed and shared the world's first and only global 30 m burned area product covering 1990–2024. It is currently the highest-resolution global burned area product. The work has produced 11 papers in journals including ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, Earth's Future, Geo-spatial Information Science, Photogrammetric Engineering & Remote Sensing, Remote Sensing, Remote Sensing Letters, and the Journal of Remote Sensing. The papers have been cited by Nature, Science, PNAS, and other leading journals; the most-cited individual paper has received 287 citations.

#### (1) Fast, high-accuracy global 30 m burned area mapping
We developed an original algorithm combining multi-source sensitive variables and machine learning for fast, high-accuracy global burned area mapping at 30 m resolution, producing the world's first and only global 30 m burned area product for 1990–2024. It is currently the highest-resolution global burned area product. The work has produced 11 papers in journals including ISPRS P&RS and Earth's Future, with citations from Nature, Science, and PNAS. #### (2) Machine-learning methods for rapid generation of global 30 m forest cover products
Combining global ecosystem zones, crowdsourced samples, and machine learning, we developed a rapid processing method for global 30 m forest cover products and established automated, continuous production. We released global 30 m forest cover products with the longest time span and highest timeliness currently available. We also mapped forests across China using domestic satellite imagery at 16 m resolution.

#### (3) Rapid generation of land-surface water products using prior knowledge
We developed a rapid land-surface water extraction method based on prior knowledge. Multiple indices exclude interfering factors, while prior knowledge guides water extraction, reducing the need for manually selected samples and increasing automation. Using available multi-temporal imagery from the target year improves the reliability of the results. Overall accuracy is 90.6%.

#### (2) CASEarth DataBank intelligent services
Supported by the China Remote Sensing Satellite Ground Station, a national major scientific facility, and developed with the Computer Network Information Center, Institute of Software, and Institute of Computing Technology of CAS, the system combines the ground station's data acquisition capabilities and archives with other Earth observation data. Data integration and standardization produce long-term, multi-source RTU satellite datasets that provide reliable, stable, and continuously updated data for Big Earth Data science, with tiered services and sharing.

The independently developed CASEarth DataBank system integrates data, computing, and services into an intelligent platform for long-term Earth observation data. It incorporates general AI methods and application-specific algorithms, using lazy computation for near-real-time cloud processing of large data volumes. This addresses difficulties in downloading Earth observation data, the specialist knowledge needed for processing, and inefficient analysis. The platform has supported a series of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) studies and established a new approach to SDG research driven by Big Earth Data. It combines expertise across disciplines and provides a complete chain from data to computing and services, offering a powerful and accessible scientific experimentation platform. It supports efficient transformation of Big Earth Data into spatial information and geoscientific knowledge, interdisciplinary work in AI and remote-sensing processing, knowledge discovery, and scientific innovation.

中国科学院空天信息创新研究院二级研究员，现任国家大科学装置-中国遥感卫星地面站党: Guojin He is a senior research professor at the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). He serves as general Party branch secretary and academic and technical lead of the China Remote Sensing Satellite Ground Station, a national major scientific facility, and as deputy director of the CAS Big Earth Data Science Data Center. He holds a CAS distinguished research appointment (core position) and an appointed professorship at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, receives the State Council Special Government Allowance, and was selected for the CAS Key Technical Talent program. His long-standing research focuses on remote-sensing information engineering. He has led key projects of the National Natural Science Foundation of China, National Key Research and Development Program projects, CAS Category A Strategic Priority Research Program tasks, and tasks of the Second Tibetan Plateau Scientific Expedition and Research program. He proposed the concept of a ready-to-use (RTU) satellite data product archive and organized rapid processing systems for multi-source satellite RTU products and CASEarth DataBank, which integrates data, computing, and intelligent Earth observation services. He developed methods for recognizing impervious surfaces, photovoltaics, urban buildings, and marine aquaculture in high-resolution imagery, producing the first nationwide 2 m marine aquaculture product and a nationwide 0.3 m photovoltaic distribution product. His team's global 30 m burned area, forest cover, and land-surface water products have been widely recognized and used. He leads the ecosystem parameter remote-sensing retrieval task of the Second Tibetan Plateau Scientific Expedition, developing quantitative retrieval methods for key ecosystem parameters. In the past five years, he has served as lead author/editor or deputy editor of two monographs, published nearly 50 papers including 34 SCI-indexed papers in Nature, RSE, TGRS, Applied Energy, and other journals, received six national invention patents, and won three provincial, ministerial, or professional society science and technology progress awards.
中国科学院空天信息创新研究院副研究员，硕士生导师，入选中国科学院青年创新促进会和: Tengfei Long is an associate research professor and master's supervisor at the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). He was selected for the CAS Youth Innovation Promotion Association and a CAS distinguished research appointment (backbone position). He serves as a Topic Editor for Remote Sensing and a member of the early-career editorial board of Remote Sensing Technology and Application. His research focuses on intelligent remote-sensing information processing and applications, including high-accuracy image registration, large-scale forest and burned area mapping, and remote sensing for human well-being, such as economic well-being, thermal environments, and public health. He developed the world's first global 30 m burned area product (GABAM), offering an order-of-magnitude improvement in spatial resolution over comparable international products.
